entry: Russian composer and teacher, a member of The Five. Rimsky-Korsakov is known for the orchestral works *Capriccio Espagnol* (1887), *Scheherazade* (1888) and *Russian Easter Festival Overture* (1888), and for his fifteen operas. He drew on Russian [[Folklore|folk]] song and [[Fairy tale|fairy-tale]] subjects, combining them with Western techniques he mastered through a three-year program of self-education. From 1871 he taught composition, [[Harmony|harmony]] and orchestration at the Saint Petersburg Conservatory, shaping a generation of Russian composers. He prepared works by [[Modest Mussorgsky]] and other members of The Five for performance, and his editing of Mussorgsky's works remains controversial. A textbook on orchestration, completed posthumously by his son-in-law Maximilian Steinberg, extended his teaching.

Russian writer, historian and critic. Karamzin introduced European sentimentalism to Russian prose, notably in the stories *Poor Liza* and *Natalia the Boyar's Daughter* (both 1792). His *Letters of a Russian Traveller*, based on a 1789 journey through [[Germany]], France, [[Switzerland]] and England, was collected in six volumes (1797–1801). In 1803 Tsar Alexander I appointed him official historiographer. He spent about two decades on the 12-volume *History of the Russian State*, a national history reaching the reign of [[Ivan the Terrible]]. His later writings favored strong monarchy, and *Memoir on Ancient and Modern Russia* (1811) criticized radical reform.

Large crocodilian of Africa's freshwater habitats. The Nile crocodile (*Crocodylus niloticus*) is present in 26 countries and is widely distributed in sub-Saharan Africa. Adult males are typically 3.5 to 5 m long, and specimens over 6.1 m have been recorded. It is Africa's largest predator and the second-largest living reptile, after the [[Saltwater crocodile]]. An ambush predator, it eats mainly fish, reptiles, birds and mammals. It is one of the most dangerous crocodiles, responsible for hundreds of human deaths each year, yet it is common and not endangered.

Proposed family of about 210 Native African languages. The languages are spoken by tens of millions of people in 17 countries across northern Africa, from Algeria to Benin in the west and from Egypt to Tanzania in the east. Joseph Greenberg named the family in *The Languages of Africa* (1963), grouping the non-click languages that did not belong to the Niger–Congo, Afroasiatic or Khoisan families. Its genetic unity is not accepted by all linguists. Glottolog (2013) does not recognize it, and Güldemann (2018) wrote that "the current state of research is not sufficient to prove the Nilo-Saharan hypothesis." Eastern Sudanic, one of its constituent groups, is estimated to date to at least the 5th millennium BC. The earliest written language associated with the family is Old [[Nubia|Nubian]], attested from the 8th to the 15th century AD.

Class of ten nuclear-powered [[Aircraft carrier|aircraft carriers]] in service with the United States Navy. The lead ship, *USS Nimitz*, was commissioned on May 3, 1975, and the tenth, *USS George H. W. Bush*, on January 10, 2009. Each ship has an overall length of 1,092 ft (333 m), and the class was the largest built until *USS Gerald R. Ford* entered service in 2017. Two nuclear reactors drive the ships at over 30 knots, and they can operate for over 20 years without refueling. Steam catapults and arresting wires launch and recover aircraft for an air wing of around 64 aircraft, mainly F/A-18E and F/A-18F Super Hornets.

American singer, pianist and civil rights activist. Born Eunice Kathleen Waymon in Tryon, North Carolina, she was known as the High Priestess of Soul. Her music drew on classical, jazz, blues, gospel and pop, and her piano playing was strongly influenced by [[Johann Sebastian Bach]]. Her debut album, *Little Girl Blue* (1958), was followed by more than 40 albums up to 1974. She became known for her work in the [[Civil rights movement|civil rights movement]] in the 1950s and 1960s, and she settled in France after the assassination of [[Martin Luther King Jr.]] in 1968.

American industrial rock band. Trent Reznor formed Nine Inch Nails in 1988 in [[Cleveland]], Ohio, and was its only permanent member until 2016, when his frequent collaborator Atticus Ross became an official member. The debut album, *Pretty Hate Machine* (1989), was followed by *The Downward Spiral* (1994) and *The Fragile* (1999). The band has sold over 20 million records and has been nominated for 13 Grammy Awards, winning for three songs, including "Wish". It was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2020.

Dystopian novel by English writer [[George Orwell]], published on June 8, 1949. Set in a fictional future in which Great Britain, now known as Airstrip One, is a province of the totalitarian superstate Oceania, the novel follows Winston Smith, a worker at the Ministry of Truth who rewrites historical records. Its themes include totalitarianism, mass surveillance and propaganda. Orwell described the book as a "satire". Terms from it, including "Big Brother", "doublethink", "thoughtcrime" and "Newspeak", have entered common usage, and the novel popularized "Orwellian" as an adjective. [[Time (magazine)|Time]] included it among the 100 best English-language novels published from 1923 to 2005. A film adaptation, *1984*, starred [[John Hurt]] and [[Richard Burton]].

Propositions for an academic disputation on indulgences, written by [[Martin Luther]] in 1517. Luther, then a professor of moral theology at the University of Wittenberg, was responding to a practice that triggered the Theses: Catholic clergy selling plenary indulgences, certificates believed to reduce punishment in [[Purgatory|purgatory]]. He argued that true repentance is inner and spiritual, not merely sacramental confession, and that indulgences led Christians to avoid repentance and acts of mercy. The Theses are considered to have launched the [[Reformation|Protestant Reformation]], although earlier proto-Protestant groups existed. Luther presented them as propositions for debate rather than settled opinions, and later clarified his views in *Explanations of the Disputation Concerning the Value of Indulgences*.

Ancient Assyrian city in [[Mesopotamia|Upper Mesopotamia]], on the eastern bank of the [[Tigris]] River in northern [[Iraq]]. Nineveh was the capital and largest city of the Neo-Assyrian Empire and was potentially the wealthiest city of the ancient world. For about fifty years it was the largest city in the world. In 612 BC, after civil war in Assyria, it was sacked by a coalition including the Babylonians, Medes and Scythians. It was never again a political or administrative center. Under [[Ashurbanipal]], its library held over 30,000 cuneiform tablets. The name is also used for the eastern half of [[Mosul]]. Tell Nabī Yūnus, a shrine to Jonah, lies within the ruins, and both the Hebrew Bible and the Quran describe Jonah as a prophet who preached to Nineveh. The city declined in the Middle Ages and was mostly abandoned by the 14th century AD after massacres and dispersal of Assyrian Christians by [[Timur]].

Sub-provincial city in northeastern [[Zhejiang]], China (pop., 2020: 9,404,283). Ningbo is the southern economic center of the Yangtze Delta megalopolis, which includes [[Shanghai]]. Its port, Ningbo–Zhoushan, is the world's busiest by cargo tonnage and was the world's third-busiest container port from 2010. Ningbo is one of China's 15 sub-provincial cities and one of five state-planning cities, a status that gives it provincial-level autonomy in economic and financial policy. Its 2022 gross domestic product was US$233.479 billion, ranked 12th among 293 Chinese cities. The city was one of the first five treaty ports opened to the West in 1842. Tianyi Pavilion, established in 1561, is the world's oldest extant private library.

Spy and infiltrator in pre-modern Japan, also called *shinobi*. Antecedents may have existed as early as the 12th century. During the [[Sengoku period]], peasant-warriors (*jizamurai*) in Iga Province and the adjacent Kōka District formed *ikki*, or leagues, for self-defense. They became known for military activity in nearby regions and sold their services as mercenaries and spies. Daimyo hired them for intelligence gathering and for disrupting enemy lines. Despite popular belief, there is little evidence that ninja were assassins, and popular culture has often romanticized them as black-clad killers with supernatural abilities. After the [[Tokugawa shogunate]] was established in the 17th century, ninja faded into obscurity.

Japanese multinational video game company, headquartered in [[Kyoto]]. It develops, publishes and manufactures video games and video game consoles. Fusajiro Yamauchi founded the company in 1889 to produce handmade hanafuda playing cards. It began making toys in the 1960s and video games in the 1970s. Its arcade game *Donkey Kong* (1981) and the [[Nintendo Entertainment System]], launched outside Japan in 1985 alongside *Super Mario Bros.*, made it internationally dominant in the 1980s. Its franchises include [[Mario]], [[The Legend of Zelda]] and [[Pokémon]]. Its consoles have sold over 870 million units worldwide, as of November 2026.

Foldable dual-screen handheld game console made by [[Nintendo]]. Released in Japan on February 26, 2011, it succeeded the [[Nintendo DS]] and offered glasses-free 3D. Its primary competitor was Sony's PlayStation Vita. Less than six months after launch, Nintendo cut its price from US$249.99 to US$169.99, and the console became one of the company's most successful handhelds in its first two years. Nintendo discontinued the 3DS line on September 16, 2020. As of December 31, 2025, the family had sold 75.94 million units.

Home video game console developed and marketed by [[Nintendo]], released in Japan on June 23, 1996. Named for its 64-bit CPU, it was Nintendo's third major home console and competed with the [[PlayStation]] and Sega Saturn. Its controller was the first to include a standard thumbstick. The console sold 32.93 million units, performing strongly in North America but less well in Japan and Europe. Its use of cartridges alienated many third-party developers, and its library numbered 388 games. The [[GameCube]] succeeded it in 2001.

Foldable handheld game console made by [[Nintendo]], released worldwide in 2004 and 2005. The "DS" stands for "Dual Screen", and its lower screen is a touchscreen. Its backward compatibility with [[Game Boy Advance]] games and strong sales led it to be widely regarded as the successor to the Game Boy line. Including the DS Lite and DSi, it sold 154 million units, making it Nintendo's best-selling console until the Switch surpassed it in 2025. The [[Nintendo 3DS]] succeeded it in 2011.

Home video game console developed and marketed by [[Nintendo]]. Released as the Famicom in Japan on July 15, 1983, and as the NES in U.S. test markets in 1985, it was Nintendo's first programmable home console. Its restrictive licensing terms led to antitrust accusations in the United States and a 1991 settlement with the Federal Trade Commission. The NES revived the American industry after the 1983 crash and pioneered the licensing model for third-party games. Nintendo sold 61.91 million consoles. *Super Mario Bros.* and [[The Legend of Zelda]] became major franchises on the system.

Hybrid video game console developed and released by [[Nintendo]] on March 3, 2017. It can be docked for home use or played as a handheld, with detachable Joy-Con controllers. It succeeded the Wii U and competed with the [[PlayStation 4]]. Later revisions include the handheld-only Switch Lite (2019) and an OLED model (2021). With over 155 million units shipped as of December 2025, it is Nintendo's best-selling console and the second-best-selling console after the [[PlayStation 2]]. The Nintendo Switch 2 was released on June 5, 2025.

Chemical element with symbol Nb and atomic number 41. Niobium is a light grey, crystalline [[Transition metal|transition metal]] that oxidizes very slowly in air, which makes it a hypoallergenic alternative to nickel in jewelry. Its name comes from Niobe, daughter of Tantalus, reflecting its similarity to [[Tantalum]]. Charles Hatchett reported it in 1801 as columbium, and Heinrich Rose named niobium in 1846. The name was officially adopted in 1949, although columbium remains in use in U.S. metallurgy. Brazil is the leading producer. Most niobium is used in alloys, especially high-strength low-alloy steels for gas pipelines, where small amounts strengthen the steel. Niobium alloys with titanium and tin are used in [[Superconductivity|superconducting]] magnets in MRI scanners.

Raised region of tissue on the surface of the [[Breast|breast]]. In lactating females, milk leaves the body through the lactiferous ducts to nurse an infant, either passively or by smooth muscle contractions. The nipple is usually surrounded by the areola, which is often darker than the surrounding skin. Male mammals also have nipples, but with less function. In humans, the nipples of both sexes can be sexually stimulated as part of sexual arousal. In many cultures, female nipples are sexualized, and their coverage is subject to social norms.

Ultimate state of liberation from suffering and rebirth in Indian religions. In Jainism, Hinduism, Buddhism and Sikhism, nirvana is the extinction of passions and release from the cycle of birth and rebirth (*saṃsāra*). The word is often translated as "extinction" or "blowing out". All these traditions describe it as perfect quietude, freedom and highest happiness. In Hindu philosophy it is the realization of the identity of Atman with [[Brahman]], depending on the tradition. In Jainism it is the release of a soul from karmic bondage. In Buddhism it is the abandonment of ten fetters, which ends rebirth by stilling the fires that drive it. Buddhist teaching links nirvana to the [[Four Noble Truths]], which hold that suffering arises from craving and can be ended by following the Noble Eightfold Path. [[The Buddha]] is said to have refused to define nirvana in speculative terms.

American rock band formed in Aberdeen, Washington, in 1987 by [[Kurt Cobain]] and Krist Novoselic. Dave Grohl joined as drummer in 1990. Nirvana was part of the [[Seattle]] grunge scene and helped popularize [[Alternative rock|alternative rock]]. Its second album, *Nevermind* (1991), included the single "Smells Like Teen Spirit" and is credited with ending the popularity of hair metal. The album was certified thirteen-times platinum in the United States. *In Utero* (1993) topped the U.S. and U.K. album charts. The band disbanded in April 1994 following Cobain's suicide. One of the best-selling music artists of all time, Nirvana has sold 60 million units in the United States alone, according to the RIAA. It was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2014.

Japanese multinational automobile manufacturer headquartered in [[Yokohama]]. It sells vehicles under the Nissan and Infiniti brands, and formerly under Datsun. Since 1999 it has been part of the Renault–Nissan–Mitsubishi Alliance. [[Renault]] held a 15% voting stake in Nissan as of November 2023. In the 2024/2025 financial year Nissan made a loss of ¥671 billion. Its new chief executive, Ivan Espinosa, announced that by 2027 Nissan will close seven factories, with the loss of 20,000 jobs, and reduce its car models from 56 to 45.

Indian film director, screenwriter and lyricist known for Hindi films. He co-directed *Chillar Party* (2011), which won two National Film Awards, and made his solo directorial debut with *Bhoothnath Returns* (2014). He wrote and directed *Dangal* (2016), starring [[Aamir Khan]], described as the highest-grossing Indian film; it won him the Filmfare Award for Best Director. *Chhichhore* (2019) won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Hindi. He also directed *Ramayana: Part 1* (2026), described as the most expensive Indian film.

Polyatomic ion, NO₃⁻, found in [[Fertilizer|fertilizers]] and explosives. Salts containing the ion are called nitrates, and nearly all inorganic nitrates are soluble in water. In nature, [[Bacteria|nitrifying bacteria]] produce nitrates from ammonia or urea. Gunpowder nitrates were historically made by fermenting urine and dung, but modern production focuses on fertilizer and chemical manufacturing. About 195 million metric tons of synthetic nitrogen fertilizers are used worldwide each year, with nitrates a significant portion. Because nitrates dissolve readily and are washed from soil by precipitation, excessive agricultural use has been linked to runoff, [[Water pollution|water pollution]] and aquatic dead zones. Excess consumption of nitrates in cured meats is associated with intestinal cancers.
